description: Registry name/address normalization; Python factlot.registry and TS @factlot/tools must agree. 'addresses' is address key version 2 (2026-11-03); 'legacy_addresses' version 1, which files built earlier keep until re-keyed. 'address_queries': how registry_search_address reads a query (mode house_number, street, or null when it has neither a house number nor a street type, and then searches nothing; tokens are the street line's words). 'address_places': the place a query names after its street line (city, state, ZIP code), read conservatively: only a state named after a city filters; a ZIP code and a city only order; unit, floor and box text and a bare two-letter or full state name name no state. 'address_place_ranks': where a match goes for a query naming a place (-1 outside its state, 0 same ZIP code, 1 same city, 2 the rest of the state). 'address_search_forms': the spellings a street line is searched by (as written first). 'address_ranges' and 'address_range_matches': a lot's house-number range [low, high, one side] and whether a query's number falls in it. 'address_street_words': the street a miss reads for its nearest house numbers. 'address_cards': what a search result carries from its label and current facts. 'address_place_with' and 'address_where_issues': the call's place parameters. 'address_queries_with_place': a query without a comma whose street line ends in a place, with the comma put in. 'address_units': the unit a label or query names, which puts the parcel naming it first. 'address_card_orders': the order of parcels sharing one label: largest improvement area first, none after, land only last, then URN. 'address_place_counties', 'address_place_differs', 'address_found' and 'address_place_misses': the counties a query's place lies in (Census tables and registry labels), which results lie outside them, and what a miss says of them.
